about: The symbolic grammar of the Connections tool. Each entry merges readings from James Jordan, Matthieu and Jonathan Pageau, Peter Leithart and the Church Fathers. 'sources' point into sources.json, where each tradition's own reading and its location are kept. Where traditions disagree, 'tension' says so; the grammar does not pick a winner.

kinds.axis: a pair of opposite poles that a story moves along
kinds.figure: a recurring creature, thing or person-type
kinds.role: a slot in a story that different figures fill
kinds.state: a condition a person or world is in
kinds.sequence: an ordered list of acts: a pattern that repeats

entries.label: Heaven and earth
entries.def: The first division of creation. Heaven is the pattern, meaning and source; earth is the matter that receives it and is shaped by it.
entries.christ: Christ joins heaven and earth in his own person (John 1:51; Eph 1:10).
entries.tension: Jordan: heaven is the blueprint and earth the copy. Pageau: heaven is meaning and earth is matter, joined in knowing. The Fathers: what is above gives its quality to what is below.

entries.label: One and many
entries.def: Movement between scattered particulars and the single identity that gathers them. Going up gathers; falling scatters.
entries.christ: Pentecost undoes Babel: many tongues, one Spirit (Acts 2).

entries.label: Center and margin
entries.def: Every ordered world has a center where heaven meets earth, and an edge where the strange, the foreign and the dangerous live.
entries.christ: Christ suffers outside the gate, at the margin, and becomes the center (Heb 13:12; Ps 118:22).
entries.tension: Pageau treats the margin as necessary and not simply evil: a healthy order leaves room for it. Jordan maps the same layout as sanctuary, homeland and outlying world.

entries.label: Going down and coming up
entries.def: The vertical movement of a story: down into water, earth, sleep or death, and back up into life, light and heaven.
entries.christ: He descended into the lower parts of the earth and ascended far above the heavens (Eph 4:9-10).

entries.label: Darkness and light
entries.def: The movement from dark to light, evening to morning, night to day. Darkness is unformed or hidden; light is meaning made clear.
entries.christ: The light shines in the darkness (John 1:5); the resurrection comes at dawn on the first day.
entries.tension: Jordan: the first darkness is unfinished, not evil. The Fathers often use darkness for the devil's region (west) in baptismal rites.

entries.label: Order and flux (Pageau's space and time)
entries.def: Stable order that holds things apart (dry land, law, work) against change that dissolves and renews (waters, rest, cycles).
entries.tension: This is Pageau's frame. Jordan has no single equivalent; his nearest terms are the land-sea line and the work-rest week.

entries.label: Clean and unclean
entries.def: The line between what may come near God and what may not, drawn by touch, food, feet and boundaries.
entries.christ: In Christ the line moves from foods to hearts (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).

entries.label: Blessing and curse
entries.def: Every symbol has a blessed form and a cursed form: tree and thorn, fruit and barrenness, upright and crawling.
entries.christ: Christ wears the crown of thorns: he takes the curse of the ground on his head (Matt 27:29; Gal 3:13).

entries.label: Grasping and receiving
entries.def: Whether a gift, office or knowledge is grabbed early or received from God in its time.
entries.christ: Christ did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped (Phil 2:6).
entries.tension: Jordan (robe of office taken too early) and Pageau (knowledge taken in all at once) reach the same axis by different roads.

entries.label: Elder and younger
entries.def: Two brothers: often an earthly, strong elder and a heavenly, weaker younger. The blessing passes to the younger.
entries.christ: Jordan: the elder is a type of the first Adam, the younger of the second Adam.

entries.label: Figure and fulfillment
entries.def: The time axis of typology: an earlier, bodily figure and a later, fuller reality. Repetition is never identical; the later is greater.
entries.christ: All the figures point to Christ: 'beginning with Moses and all the Prophets' (Luke 24:27).

entries.label: Land and sea
entries.def: Dry, ordered ground against restless water. The sea is the edge of the world and what threatens to swallow the land.
entries.christ: Christ walks on the sea and stills it (Mark 4:39; 6:48); in the new creation there is no more sea (Rev 21:1).
entries.tension: Jordan: the sea is mainly the Gentile nations. Pageau: the sea is flux and confusion. Both read Rev 21:1 as the end of that division.

entries.label: Male and female
entries.def: The human form of heaven and earth: one gives seed and word, the other receives, nourishes and brings it to birth.
entries.christ: Christ and the Church are the great mystery behind marriage (Eph 5:32).

entries.label: Right hand and left hand
entries.def: Right is blessing, strength and accurate action; left is the loose, weak, set-aside side, near the margin.

entries.label: North and south
entries.def: Biblical geography read vertically: the north is height, source and identity; the south (Egypt) is depth, food and the body.
entries.tension: Jordan: north is the direction of God's throne. Pageau: going up north for identity and down south for goods.

entries.label: West and east
entries.def: East is the side of light and Paradise; exile runs east of Eden, and conversion turns from west to east.
entries.tension: In Genesis, going east is going away from Eden; in the baptismal rite (Cyril), facing east is turning to Paradise.

entries.label: Head and body
entries.def: The head gives meaning and direction; the body gives strength and carries it out. Societies are bodies with heads.
entries.christ: Christ is head of the body, the Church (Col 1:18). Tyconius' first rule: head and body can speak as one person.

entries.label: Garden and city
entries.def: History runs from a planted garden to a built city. The city can be the rebel's counterfeit or God's finished house.
entries.christ: The New Jerusalem comes down with the garden and tree of life inside it (Rev 22:1-2).

entries.label: Highest heaven
entries.def: God's throne-house, made first and unseen, modeled on earth by the Most Holy Place.
entries.christ: Christ entered heaven itself, the true holy place (Heb 9:24).

entries.label: The firmament (the sky)
entries.def: The visible sky between the waters above and below: a shell that dimly shows the highest heaven; socially, the rulers.

entries.label: The deep (the first waters)
entries.def: Waters before or beneath order: dark, unformed, full of possibility. They return in the flood and under every sea crossing.
entries.christ: Christ descends to the abyss and rises from it (Rom 10:7). Tertullian: these waters were the first seat of the Spirit and the figure of baptism.
entries.tension: The traditions do not agree. Jordan: the first deep is unfinished, not evil. Pageau (Matthieu): flux and confusion, not evil in itself. Jonathan Pageau and Revelation: chaos and the monster's home. The Fathers: life-bearing and holy at creation, deadly in judgment. Tag the sense on each occurrence.

entries.label: Dry land
entries.def: Ordered ground raised out of the waters: where things are stable, named and fit to live on.

entries.label: Holy mountain
entries.def: A high place where heaven and earth meet: God comes down, man goes up and sees the pattern, and rivers flow out.
entries.christ: The Transfiguration and the Sermon on the Mount; the stone cut without hands becomes a mountain that fills the earth (Dan 2:35).
entries.tension: Jordan and Pageau make Ararat a holy mountain. The Fathers read here do not use Ararat as a type; for them the mountain is Christ or the Church.

entries.label: Garden sanctuary
entries.def: The innermost guarded place where God and man meet, with the tree at its center and rivers flowing out.
entries.christ: Christ is betrayed in a garden and buried in a garden; the Church is the new Paradise (Irenaeus, Cyril).

entries.label: Homeland
entries.def: The middle zone around the sanctuary: the inherited land of rest, kept by keeping the law.

entries.label: The outer world
entries.def: The lands beyond the homeland, reached by rivers and roads: the place of work, trade, nations and danger.

entries.label: Wilderness
entries.def: The unformed land between bondage and inheritance: a place of testing, hunger and God's direct provision.
entries.christ: Christ goes from the Jordan into the wilderness for forty days (Matt 4:1-2).

entries.label: House of bondage
entries.def: The foreign land where God's people are enslaved and from which every exodus begins.
entries.christ: 'Out of Egypt I called my son' (Matt 2:15).

entries.label: City of man
entries.def: A city built for self-protection and a name, without God: a counterfeit sanctuary and counterfeit mountain.

entries.label: Gate
entries.def: The base of the ladder or the edge of a holy place: where heaven meets earth and where judgment is given.

entries.label: The pit
entries.def: The low place: pit, prison, grave or Sheol, where the righteous are put and from which God raises them.
entries.christ: Joseph and Jonah are raised from the pit; Christ from the tomb (Matt 12:40).

entries.label: Well
entries.def: Water in the dry land where life is given and brides are found.
entries.christ: Christ meets the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well (John 4).

entries.label: New Jerusalem
entries.def: The final city coming down from heaven: sanctuary, land and bride at once, with the garden and tree inside.

entries.label: Ladder between heaven and earth
entries.def: Any upright thing that links earth to heaven: tree, mountain, ladder, pillar, altar, staff. Its foot is the gate.
entries.christ: 'You will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man' (John 1:51).

entries.label: Counterfeit ladder
entries.def: A ladder to heaven built up from below by man's own effort: Babel, the ziggurat, the proud tree. God cuts it down.

entries.label: Tree of life
entries.def: The tree at the center: life given as a gift at the start, the axis joining heaven and earth.
entries.christ: Christian art and the Fathers identify it with the cross and with Christ himself.

entries.label: Tree of the knowledge of good and evil
entries.def: The tree withheld for a time: knowledge and judgment that must be received in its time, not seized.
entries.christ: Irenaeus: the disobedience at a tree is undone by obedience on a tree.
entries.tension: Jordan: banned for a time, not forever (judicial maturity). Pageau: holds a good and a bad mediator together.

entries.label: The cross
entries.def: The tree on which Christ died: the true ladder, the altar, and the answer to the tree of the fall.
entries.christ: Itself.

entries.label: Saving wood
entries.def: Wood God uses to save: the ark, Moses' rod, the wood at Marah, the bronze serpent's pole, Elisha's stick.
entries.christ: All point to the cross (Justin, Cyril, Ambrose; in the Patrista corpus see Cyril, Catechetical Lectures 13).

entries.label: Altar
entries.def: A small holy mountain of earth or stone where something is offered up to God; its four horns are the earth's corners.

entries.label: The rock
entries.def: God as unmoving rock: refuge, foundation, and the rock struck in the wilderness that gives water.
entries.christ: 'The rock was Christ' (1 Cor 10:4); water and blood flow from his pierced side (John 19:34).

entries.label: Foundation stone, stumbling stone, capstone
entries.def: The stone that orders a building, the odd stone that will not fit and brings it down, and the rejected stone made head.
entries.christ: Christ is all three: foundation, stone of stumbling, and the rejected stone made head of the corner (1 Pet 2:6-8).

entries.label: The vessel through the waters
entries.def: A closed wooden vessel that carries the chosen one through the waters of death: Noah's ark, Moses' basket.
entries.christ: The ark is the Church and its wood the cross (Cyril, Ambrose). Hebrew: the same rare word (tevah) names Noah's ark and Moses' basket.

entries.label: Glory cloud
entries.def: God's visible presence: cloud, fire, light and thunder that lead the people, cover the mountain and fill the house.
entries.christ: The cloud overshadows Mary (Luke 1:35) and the Transfiguration (Matt 17:5).

entries.label: The dove
entries.def: The clean bird sent over the waters that returns with a sign of new land; the Spirit descending.
entries.christ: The Spirit descends on Christ as a dove at the Jordan (Matt 3:16). Tertullian (Bapt. 8) links Noah's dove and the Jordan dove.
entries.note: The prophet Jonah's name is 'dove' (H3124); Peter is Bar-Jona (G920), 'son of Jonah/dove'.

entries.label: The raven
entries.def: The dark bird that goes out and does not return: it stays with the dead world.
entries.tension: The ravens that feed Elijah carry the opposite sense: the same figure, used for good.

entries.label: Olive and oil
entries.def: The olive leaf of peace after the flood; olive oil that anoints and gives light.
entries.christ: Christ means 'anointed one'; he prays on the Mount of Olives (Luke 22:39).

entries.label: Sun, moon and stars
entries.def: The lights of day four rule time and stand for rulers; their darkening means a ruling order falls.
entries.christ: The Sun of righteousness (Mal 4:2); the morning star (Rev 22:16).

entries.label: The bow in the cloud
entries.def: God's war-bow hung up in the cloud: the sign that wrath has turned to peace, and a crown around his throne.

entries.label: Garment and robe
entries.def: Clothing as covering and office: fig leaves, God-given skins, the robe of rule, the white robe put on in baptism.
entries.christ: We put on Christ in baptism (Gal 3:27); his seamless robe is not torn (John 19:23-24).

entries.label: Bread and wine
entries.def: Grain and grape worked into food: bread for strength and work, wine for rest and gladness.
entries.christ: The Eucharist; Melchizedek's bread and wine as its figure (Cyprian, Ambrose).

entries.label: Bread from heaven
entries.def: Food that comes down from heaven in the wilderness, enough for each day.
entries.christ: 'I am the bread that came down from heaven' (John 6:41).

entries.label: The seed
entries.def: A small beginning that contains the whole: the promised child, the word, the line that carries the promise.
entries.christ: 'To your offspring, who is Christ' (Gal 3:16).

entries.label: Blood
entries.def: Life poured out: it cries from the ground, marks the doorposts, seals the covenant, and must not be eaten.
entries.christ: Water and blood from Christ's side (John 19:34); his blood speaks better than Abel's (Heb 12:24).

entries.label: Fire
entries.def: Heaven's fire that judges, refines and consumes the offering; the opposite extreme to the flood.
entries.christ: Christ baptizes with the Holy Spirit and fire (Matt 3:11).

entries.label: River from the sanctuary
entries.def: Water flowing out from God's dwelling to water the world, growing deeper as it goes.
entries.christ: 'Out of his heart will flow rivers of living water' (John 7:38-39).

entries.label: House of God as a model of the world
entries.def: A God-designed house that pictures heaven and earth, the people and the person at once: ark, tabernacle, temple.
entries.christ: 'He was speaking about the temple of his body' (John 2:21).

entries.label: The serpent
entries.def: The crafty creature at the edge of the garden who tempts to grasp early; also the bronze serpent lifted up to heal.
entries.christ: 'As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up' (John 3:14).
entries.tension: Augustine's rule: one symbol, opposite senses. Tag the sense on each occurrence.

entries.label: The monster of the deep
entries.def: The creature in the waters that swallows: Leviathan, the dragon, Jonah's great fish; death and the devil.
entries.christ: Christ is in the heart of the earth three days as Jonah was in the fish (Matt 12:40).

entries.label: The beast
entries.def: A man or power that grasps at godhood and becomes less than human: a predator, a tyrant-empire.
entries.christ: The Son of Man receives the kingdom from the beasts (Dan 7:13-14).

entries.label: The lamb in our place
entries.def: The animal killed in place of the people, whose blood turns away death.
entries.christ: 'Behold, the Lamb of God' (John 1:29).

entries.label: Mediator from above
entries.def: A heavenly agent that comes down onto the water, the offering or the chosen one and makes it live: Spirit, dove, voice, fire, angel.
entries.christ: At the Jordan: the Spirit as a dove and the Father's voice (Matt 3:16-17).

entries.label: Man between heaven and earth
entries.def: The human whose task is to stand between heaven and earth: to bring heaven's pattern down and lift creation up.
entries.christ: One mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus (1 Tim 2:5).

entries.label: Head of a new world
entries.def: The one through whom a new world begins after judgment: he repeats Adam's place with more glory.
entries.christ: The last Adam (1 Cor 15:45). Irenaeus: Christ sums up Adam in himself (recapitulation).

entries.label: The righteous remnant
entries.def: The one righteous man with his household, or the faithful few, kept alive through judgment to seed a new world.

entries.label: Guardian of the holy place
entries.def: The one charged to keep the sanctuary and the bride from intruders: Adam first, then cherubim, priests, the Church.
entries.christ: The good shepherd who guards the sheep against the wolf (John 10:11-12).

entries.label: The bride
entries.def: The woman placed in the garden, whom the serpent or tyrant tries to take, and whom the bridegroom washes and claims.
entries.christ: The Church is the bride, washed with water by the word (Eph 5:26).

entries.label: The bridegroom
entries.def: The one who comes for the bride, washes and adorns her, and brings her into his house.
entries.christ: John the Baptist: 'The one who has the bride is the bridegroom' (John 3:29).

entries.label: The tyrant
entries.def: The foreign lord who enslaves God's people, seizes the bride, is struck by God and drowned or overthrown.
entries.christ: Herod plays Pharaoh at Christ's birth (Matt 2:16).

entries.label: The deliverer sent
entries.def: A leader sent by God into the land of bondage to bring the people out through water.
entries.christ: Cyril (Mystagogical Lecture 1): Moses sent to Egypt, Christ sent into the world.

entries.label: The forerunner
entries.def: The servant who goes ahead to prepare the way with repentance and water, and points to one greater.
entries.christ: John the Baptist: 'He must increase, but I must decrease' (John 3:30).

entries.label: The younger son chosen
entries.def: The younger brother who receives the blessing in place of the firstborn.

entries.label: The firstborn passed over
entries.def: The elder, often strong and earthly, who loses the blessing by contempt, violence or failure.

entries.label: The barren mother
entries.def: The woman who cannot bear until God opens her womb, at a turning point of the story.
entries.christ: The line runs to Elizabeth and then to the virgin who conceives (Luke 1:36-37).

entries.label: The stranger
entries.def: The outsider who carries change into the story: the foreign woman, the spy, the captive maid, the Gentile convert.
entries.christ: Tamar, Rahab and Ruth stand in Christ's genealogy (Matt 1:3-5).
entries.tension: Pageau: the strange woman brings ruin and renewal. Ambrose: the captive maid is the Church of the Gentiles.

entries.label: Man of the margin
entries.def: A strong figure of the edge, marked by hair, skins or exile: hunter, wanderer, prophet. Power or holiness, depending on use.
entries.christ: John the Baptist in camel's hair at the Jordan (Matt 3:4).
entries.tension: This is Pageau's category; Jordan does not name it.

entries.label: The fool
entries.def: A low or upside-down figure who exposes the king's nakedness; in the good case the low one raised up.
entries.christ: The mock king crowned with thorns (Matt 27:27-31).

entries.label: The city-builder
entries.def: The rebel who takes creation without thanks and builds a city and a name for himself.

entries.label: The servant raised up
entries.def: The faithful servant who is stripped, enslaved or imprisoned, serves well from below, and is robed by the king.
entries.christ: Taking the form of a servant, he humbled himself; therefore God highly exalted him (Phil 2:7-9).

entries.label: Priest, king and prophet
entries.def: Three offices of the human mediator: the priest guards, the king rules and builds, the prophet stands in God's council.
entries.christ: Christ holds all three offices; Tertullian: the name 'Christ' comes from the anointing of priests and kings.

entries.label: Separate
entries.def: Divide one thing from another to make room for order: light from dark, waters from waters, a people from the nations.

entries.label: Name
entries.def: Give a creature or person its identity by speaking. Naming comes before rule.

entries.label: Go down
entries.def: Go down into water, pit, sleep, Egypt or death. Also used for heaven coming down.

entries.label: Come up
entries.def: Come up out of water, pit, grave or exile into light; or go up the mountain to God.

entries.label: Pass through the water
entries.def: Cross or be carried through water that kills others: the flood, the sea, the river, the font.

entries.label: Send out a messenger to test the world
entries.def: Send a bird, spy or servant out to see whether the new land is ready, and wait for a sign.

entries.label: Grasp too early
entries.def: Take what will be given later: the fruit, the father's robe, the blessing, the kingdom.

entries.label: Eat
entries.def: Take something into the body and so into oneself: the forbidden fruit, the Passover, manna, the Supper.

entries.label: Cover and clothe
entries.def: Cover nakedness, by man's own effort (fig leaves) or by God's gift (skins, robe).

entries.label: Drive out
entries.def: Send out from a holier zone to a lower one: from the garden, the land, the city.

entries.label: Deep sleep
entries.def: God puts a man into deep sleep (tardemah) and, while he sleeps, divides, makes covenant or brings forth.
entries.christ: From the side of Christ asleep in death, the Church is formed, as Eve from Adam's side (a common patristic reading).

entries.label: Offer up
entries.def: Lift something from earth to God: sacrifice, smoke, tithe, firstfruits, praise.

entries.label: Pour down and anoint
entries.def: Pour oil or Spirit from above onto a stone, a priest or a king, to make it holy and set it in office.

entries.label: Give thanks
entries.def: Receive a gift back from God's hand before using it. Jordan: this step separates faithful work from rebellion.

entries.label: See and judge
entries.def: Look at what has been made and give a verdict: 'it was good', or judgment.

entries.label: Build God's house
entries.def: After victory, build a house for God from the spoils and set up worship.

entries.label: Strike and open
entries.def: Strike the rock, the sea or the shepherd, and water or life flows out.

entries.label: Mix what should stay apart
entries.def: Join things that God kept distinct: sons of God and daughters of men, holy and common, Israel and idols.

entries.label: Rest
entries.def: Stop work on the seventh day and let the world return to God's hand.
entries.christ: Christ rests in the tomb on the sabbath and rises on the first day.

entries.label: Nakedness
entries.def: Being uncovered: first innocence, then after sin the shame of being exposed without office or wisdom.
entries.christ: Christ is stripped on the cross; we are clothed with him.

entries.label: Exile
entries.def: Living outside the land among strangers: losing guidance, then support, then the land itself.

entries.label: Without form
entries.def: The state before order (tohu wa-bohu), to which judgment returns a corrupt world before it is formed again.

entries.label: Glory
entries.def: The goal of the world: creation grown into heaven's likeness, shining with God's light.

entries.label: Three and the third day
entries.def: The third day is the day of rising after death or of a new start after a test.
entries.christ: Raised on the third day according to the Scriptures (1 Cor 15:4).

entries.label: Four
entries.def: The four corners of the earth: rivers, cherub faces, altar horns, the arms of the cross.

entries.label: Six and seven
entries.def: Six is work and measure; seven is the rest and release that completes it and starts the new.

entries.label: Twelve
entries.def: The full people of God: twelve tribes, stones, loaves, apostles, gates.

entries.label: Forty
entries.def: The period of testing or waiting before something new is given: days of rain, years in the wilderness, days of fasting.
entries.christ: Christ's forty days in the wilderness (Matt 4:2).

entries.label: Seventy
entries.def: The nations of the world, counted in the table of Genesis 10.
entries.christ: Jesus sends out seventy (Luke 10:1).

entries.label: Through the waters to new creation
entries.def: A chosen one goes down into water that kills, is carried or brought through, comes up onto new ground, and heaven answers.

steps.note: into the water, the pit or the sea
heaven answers: dove, voice, cloud, fire
a new name or a word from heaven

entries.christ: The Fathers' master chain: creation waters, flood, Red Sea, Jordan, Christ's baptism, the font (Tertullian, Cyril, Ambrose).

entries.label: Undoing and remaking a world
entries.def: An ordered world is corrupted, returned to formlessness by judgment, and formed again through a chosen one.

steps.note: the order is corrupted
God sees the corruption
the world is returned to formlessness
a new order is formed

entries.label: The life of a covenant world
entries.def: Jordan's repeating shape of history. Each round rises higher until Christ breaks the cycle.

steps.note: decline of the old world; God announces judgment and a new world through a prophet
exodus: God brings his people out
establishment: new laws, names and a sanctuary
history and decline: God tests faithfulness
judgment, which is also the announcement of the next world

entries.label: Exodus
entries.def: God's people are brought out of bondage through water and testing into a new land, carrying spoils to build God's house.

steps.note: the people go down or are driven into a foreign land
the tyrant enslaves them or takes the bride
God strikes the tyrant
testing and bread from heaven
the spoils furnish God's house

entries.label: The fall
entries.def: A tempter urges grasping before the time; the gift is seized, eyes open to nakedness, a covering is made, and exile follows.

steps.note: the tempter's 'why wait?'
nakedness exposed and covered
God comes and judges

entries.label: The fall undone in reverse
entries.def: Irenaeus: Christ repeats the steps of the fall and reverses each one with the same instrument.

steps.note: a virgin hears an angel's word and obeys (Eve disobeyed)
temptation refused in the wilderness (Adam yielded in the garden)
obedience on a tree (disobedience at a tree)
from the side of the sleeping man the bride comes

entries.tension: Irenaeus' 'recapitulation' (Christ replays Adam) differs from Tyconius' 'recapitulation' (a flashback in the story). Keep them as separate tags.

entries.label: The bride taken and returned
entries.def: A ruler takes the bride; the weak deceive him or God strikes him; the bride is returned with spoils.

steps.note: famine or exile brings the family under a foreign lord
the bride is taken
God strikes the ruler's house
the ruler blames the righteous
the bride is returned with spoils

entries.label: The younger chosen over the elder
entries.def: The firstborn forfeits the blessing; it passes to the younger, often by an odd act or a crossing of hands.

steps.note: two brothers stand before God or the father
the younger is accepted

entries.label: Stripped, humbled, then robed
entries.def: The faithful one is stripped and thrown down, serves well from below, refuses to grasp, and is robed and raised by the king.

steps.note: robed too early, or given a robe
stripped and thrown down
refuses illicit power
interprets God's word
robed and set over the house

entries.label: Heaven comes down, earth is offered up
entries.def: Pageau's exchange: heaven sends down a seed, word or bread; earth sends up an offering; a mediator joins them at the mountain or house.

steps.note: word, seed, manna, fire or oil comes down
flesh, smoke or praise goes up
the meeting place is set up

entries.label: Up the mountain, down to build
entries.def: A man goes up the holy mountain, sees heaven's pattern, comes down and builds the earth after it.

steps.note: he sees the pattern

entries.label: The work of a week
entries.def: Jordan's pattern of work: take hold, give thanks, break and reshape, give out, be judged, rest and enjoy.

steps.note: take hold (in good sense: receive)
break and reshape
distribute

entries.tension: Without the thanksgiving step, Jordan reads the same pattern as Cain's: the city of man.

entries.label: Exile and return
entries.def: The law is broken; heaven's guidance, then the earth's support, then the land is lost; the people wander and are brought back.

steps.note: the law is broken
wandering among strangers
return
